metadata.title: Theo Johnson - Four targets, zero catches in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Johnson played 16 of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps but did not haul in any of his four targets during Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
metadata.analysis: All four of Johnson's targets came in the first half, three of which were in the opening quarter. The third-year tight end failed to record a catch, but he did log a tackle on Trent McDuffie after the latter intercepted Jameis Winston midway through the second quarter. Johnson is firmly behind Isaiah Likely on the depth chart, though all of the Giants pass catchers figure to see their production dip with Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart, the latter of whom could miss the rest of the season due to a knee injury.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson - Limited offensive production in Week 1
metadata.description: Johnson caught his only target for nine yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Johnson operated as a clear second-fiddle to Isaiah Likely at tight end in Week 1, with the latter reeling in all eight of his targets for 78 yards and two scores in the game. Johnson was only on the field for 32 of the team's 69 offensive snaps, and as long as Likely is available, he won't have much fantasy appeal this season.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson held to one catch Sunday
metadata.description: Theo Johnson caught just one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: New York didn't get their tight end very involved on Sunday night, as he was held to just one catch in the team's win over their divisional rival. Isaiah Likely proved himself to be far and away their most talented receiver at the tight end position in this matchup, so Johnson will likely continue to be relegated to a blocking and depth role for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson (shoulder) logs full practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Theo Johnson (shoulder) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: It looks like the Giants will have Johnson available to play for them on Sunday, as he was able to log a full practice to start the week on Wednesday. He won't carry any fantasy value himself but should serve as a nice depth option for Jaxson Dart moving forward.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson - Full practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Johnson (shoulder) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Johnson is coming off a 2025 regular season in which he posted a 45-528-5 line on 74 targets in 15 games, but the arrival of TE Isaiah Likely via free agency has provided the former with some competition at the position ahead of his third pro campaign. With the shoulder injury he picked up in an Aug. 24 practice behind Johnson, he'll focus on being a regular part of the Giants offense in Sunday's Week 1 matchup with the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson's Redraft Stock Has Slipped
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Theo Johnson still has a role, but the fantasy case has taken a hit. Johnson was productive last season, finishing with 45 catches for 528 yards and five touchdowns, yet Isaiah Likely has been the more prominent receiving option throughout camp. Likely caught six passes during live work in the Aug. 20 joint practice with Miami and was described by Jordan Raanan as one of Jaxson Dart's favorite targets. Johnson, meanwhile, had a quiet camp before a shoulder injury cost him additional practice time late in August. Head coach John Harbaugh has said Johnson should be ready for Week 1, so the injury itself is not the main concern. The bigger issue is where the targets are going. RotoBaller has Likely at TE15 in its September half-PPR rankings and Johnson at TE42. Johnson should still see the field, especially in two-tight-end sets, but he is looking more like a secondary option in the passing game than a breakout candidate.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson (shoulder) practices in non-contact jersey
metadata.description: Theo Johnson practiced on Tuesday wearing a non-contact jersey.
metadata.analysis: Johnson will have the next week and a half to get fully healthy for the start of the season.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson - Donning non-contact jersey at practice
metadata.description: Johnson (shoulder) is participating in Monday's practice in a non-contact jersey, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: Johnson was injured in practice last Monday and continues to deal with the injury, though his return to action would suggest the tight end is on track to play Week 1 against the Cowboys. Johnson figures to work mostly as a blocker this season after the Giants signed Isaiah Likely to a contract over the offseason.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson Wears Non-Contact Jersey at Monday's Practice
metadata.description: New York Giants tight end Theo Johnson (shoulder) was wearing a red, non-contact jersey at the team's practice on Monday, according to Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News. Johnson is still not a full-go this week after injuring his shoulder in practice last Monday. The fact that the 25-year-old was even out there on Monday suggests that he should be fine for the Week 1 season opener on Sunday night, Sept. 13, against the division-rival Dallas Cowboys. The former fourth-round selection in the 2024 NFL draft from Penn State improved in his second season in 2025, catching 45 of his 74 targets for 528 yards and five touchdowns in 15 starts after posting a 29-331-1 line in 12 games as a rookie. Johnson could have a decent role in his third NFL campaign in a Giants offense that figures to utilize plenty of two-tight-end sets, but unless Isaiah Likely misses time with an injury, his fantasy football ceiling will be low in an offense that wants to ground and pound. At RotoBaller, Johnson is ranked as the No. 42 fantasy TE, so he should only be drafted for depth in two-TE leagues.

metadata.title: Theo Johnson - Dealing with shoulder injury
metadata.description: Johnson missed Wednesday's practice due to a shoulder injury, Evan Barnes of Newsday reports.
metadata.analysis: Johnson made an early exit Monday and hasn't yet returned, but there's been no indication of a serious injury that would jeopardize his Week 1 status. Giants coach John Harbaugh said Wednesday that Johnson will be ready for the season opener, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
